items.title: Expand the contract for multi-currency amounts, exchange groups and reporting currency
items.outcome: The published specification carries currency, exchange groups, quoted rates and reporting-currency derivation as first-class wire concepts, so every generated client speaks multi-currency identically instead of Android and the backend agreeing privately.
items.context: Multi-currency currently appears only in the ledger ticket and an Android rendering ticket. Without a contract slice the web application and any future client would have to infer currency behaviour, and a cross-currency total could be produced by a client that was never told it is meaningless.
scope: Currency code required on every amount component, with no default and no inference
Linked exchange group representation with quoted rate, rate source, rate instant and explicit fee
Reporting-currency request parameter and a derivation object on every converted figure
Explicit absence of any scalar cross-currency total in list, summary and report responses
Generated client guidance stating that formatting is a render-time concern and never a wire concern
acceptance_criteria: No response schema exposes a total that mixes currencies without a per-currency breakdown and a derivation object
Every converted figure carries the rate, the rate source, the rate instant and the fee that produced it
Generated Kotlin and TypeScript clients round-trip a multi-currency payload without loss, proven by a cross-language test
The TypeScript surface keeps the canonical decimal string as the public type; no bigint appears on any generated boundary
The additions are additive: an existing single-currency client compiles and behaves identically against the new specification
A contract test rejects any endpoint that accepts an amount without a currency code
contracts_schema: Currency, exchange group, quoted rate and reporting derivation components defined once and referenced everywhere
security_privacy: Rate sources are named in the contract so a disputed figure can be investigated without server access
No new personal data field is introduced by the multi-currency additions
observability: Specification change published with a version and a compatibility report for every generated client
tests: Cross-language round-trip test over multi-currency payloads
Contract test asserting no bare amount and no scalar cross-currency total exists
Backwards-compatibility test running the previous client against the new specification
rollout_rollback: Published as an additive specification version; clients adopt on their own schedule
Rollback is republishing the previous specification version, which remains compatible
non_goals: Rendering and locale formatting, which the client tickets own
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo contracts. Owns the specification additions and the generated packages. The api and client repositories consume the published version.

items.title: Implement the multi-currency ledger with clearing accounts, linked groups and quoted rates
items.outcome: As a user with money in more than one currency, I can hold accounts in each, record an exchange between them, and see the rate and the fee that were actually applied.
items.context: The ledger deliberately reserved this structure and deferred the feature so the single-currency invariants stayed simple and enforceable. Implementing it later is only safe if the reserved structures are used as designed and no existing stored amount changes.
scope: Per-currency clearing accounts activated as real accounts
Linked exchange groups representing a cross-currency movement as connected single-currency transactions
Quoted rate, rate source and explicit fee stored on every exchange
Reporting currency selection with the conversion derivation exposed
Migration that leaves every existing stored amount unchanged
acceptance_criteria: Each transaction remains single-currency; a cross-currency movement is a linked group whose entries sum to zero per currency, enforced by the database
Every converted figure traces to a stored rate, a rate source and a stated fee
The rate is stored at the time of the exchange and is never recomputed from a later rate
Existing single-currency users see identical stored amounts and derived balances after migration
Reporting in a selected currency exposes its derivation rather than presenting a bare converted number
All arithmetic agrees with the independent model, including rounding on conversion
No endpoint returns a scalar total that mixes currencies; every mixed view is a per-currency breakdown with a stated derivation
contracts_schema: Implements the multi-currency additions to the published ledger contract additively
security_privacy: Rate sources are recorded so a disputed figure can be investigated
No currency conversion is executed on the user's behalf; the application records what happened
observability: Publishes exchange group counts and per-currency constraint violation attempts
tests: Per-currency zero-sum constraint tests
Migration equivalence test on existing data
Rate provenance test
Independent model agreement on conversion rounding
rollout_rollback: Behind a flag; single-currency behaviour is unchanged with the flag off
Rollback disables multi-currency entry; existing groups remain readable and correct
non_goals: Executing conversion or holding balances, permanently

items.title: Build the Android localization framework and INR-first money rendering
items.outcome: As a user, amounts, dates and numbers are shown the way my locale writes them, with the Indian rupee as the default presentation and the Indian digit grouping convention, and the application text can be translated without a code change.
items.context: Rendering is currently unspecified, which is how a domestic currency ends up formatted with foreign grouping rules on the screen where someone reads their debt. Formatting must also stay strictly at the render boundary so no formatted string leaks into the domain layer. This is MVP work for a single-currency product and depends on nothing in E30: currency selection and multi-currency presentation are separated into T-GLO-04, which does depend on the server-side multi-currency work.
scope: Localization framework with externalised strings and plural handling
Locale-aware number, date and currency formatting at the render boundary only
Domestic currency as the default presentation with the correct grouping convention
Layout resilience for longer translated strings and right-to-left readiness
acceptance_criteria: Every user-facing string is externalised; a hard-coded display string fails a build check
The domestic currency renders with the correct grouping convention, verified by snapshot tests
No formatted monetary string exists in the domain layer, enforced by a static check
Layouts remain readable with substantially longer translated strings and at the largest text scale
Screen readers announce amounts with their currency unambiguously
contracts_schema: Consumes the published money representation; formatting is derived from it and never parsed from a display string
security_privacy: Locale is a presentation setting and is not sent to any external service with financial data
observability: Records locale distribution as a coarse metric without user identifiers
tests: Formatting snapshot tests per supported locale
Hard-coded string build check
Domain layer formatting static check
Long-string layout test
Accessibility announcement test
rollout_rollback: Ships with the domestic locale enabled; additional locales are added behind a flag as translations land
Rollback returns to the domestic locale without affecting stored data
non_goals: Translation content itself, which is a separate content activity
Server-side conversion, which the ledger ticket owns
Currency selection and multi-currency presentation, which T-GLO-04 owns
The quality gate that verifies this rendering, which T-QA-08 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo android. Owns the localization framework and rendering. Stored amounts are never touched.

items.title: Render multi-currency balances, exchanges and reporting currency in the web application
items.outcome: As a user with money in more than one currency, the web application shows each balance in its own currency, shows an exchange as a linked pair with the rate and fee that were applied, and never presents a mixed-currency total as a single number.
items.context: Multi-currency support was scoped to the ledger and to Android only, which would leave the web application silently wrong for the same user. The web slice makes the wire contract visible on the second client and keeps formatting at the render boundary.
scope: Locale-aware money rendering at the render boundary only, driven by the published wire representation
Per-currency balance grouping with no scalar cross-currency total anywhere in the interface
Exchange presentation showing the linked pair, the quoted rate, the rate source and the explicit fee
Reporting-currency selector that shows the derivation behind every converted figure
Externalised strings, plural handling and layout resilience for longer translations and right-to-left readiness
acceptance_criteria: No screen displays a total that mixes currencies without a per-currency breakdown, verified by a component test over a mixed portfolio
Every converted figure exposes its rate, rate source, rate instant and fee on inspection
No formatted monetary string exists outside the render boundary, enforced by a static check
Currency selection changes presentation only and never changes a stored amount, proven by an end-to-end assertion on the request payload
Amounts are announced unambiguously with their currency by a screen reader and meet the stated accessibility conformance target
No bigint crosses a server component or JSON boundary; the canonical decimal string is parsed once at the render boundary
contracts_schema: Consumes the published multi-currency contract; the client parses no display string and infers no currency
security_privacy: Locale and reporting-currency choices are presentation settings and are not sent to any external service with financial data
observability: Reporting-currency selection and derivation inspection counts published without amounts
tests: Component tests over a mixed-currency portfolio asserting no scalar total
Static check for formatted money outside the render boundary and for bigint on any boundary
Accessibility test asserting currency is announced with the amount
rollout_rollback: Shipped behind the same flag as the multi-currency ledger; single-currency users see no change
Rollback hides the currency selector and falls back to domestic presentation with no stored data change
non_goals: Translation content, which is a separate content activity
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo web. Owns rendering, the selector and the localization wiring. Stored amounts and server derivation are untouched.

items.title: Add Android currency selection and multi-currency presentation
items.outcome: Once the server supports more than one currency, a user can choose a presentation currency and see multi-currency holdings rendered correctly, without any stored amount ever being changed.
items.context: Currency selection was bundled with the Android localization framework, which made an MVP formatting task depend on the whole multi-currency server programme. Splitting it lets INR-first rendering ship in the numbered schedule while the multi-currency surface waits for the ledger and contract work it genuinely needs.
scope: Presentation currency selection and its persistence
Multi-currency holdings presentation, including per-currency subtotals and the rule for a mixed-currency view
Explicit statement in the interface of which figures are converted and as at what rate and time
Rendering of a converted figure as derived rather than authoritative
States from the T-UX-01 taxonomy that apply when a rate is stale or unavailable
acceptance_criteria: Changing the presentation currency changes presentation only; a test asserts every stored amount and every ledger entry is unchanged
A view containing more than one currency shows per-currency subtotals and never adds different currencies into one number without a stated conversion
Every converted figure states the rate and the time it was taken, and is visually distinguishable from an unconverted figure
A stale or unavailable rate produces the stale state from the T-UX-01 taxonomy rather than a silently outdated number
Screen readers announce each amount with its currency unambiguously, including in a mixed-currency view
contracts_schema: Consumes the multi-currency and rate shapes published by T-CON-05 through the generated client; no rate is fetched or computed locally
security_privacy: Presentation currency is a user preference and carries no financial consequence; the ticket introduces no new data collection
observability: Presentation currency selections and stale-rate occurrences are counted, so an unusable rate source is visible
tests: Stored-amount immutability test on currency change
Mixed-currency subtotal test
Converted-figure labelling test
Stale-rate state test
Screen reader announcement test in a mixed-currency view
rollout_rollback: Ships behind a flag that stays off until the server-side multi-currency work is live
Rollback hides the selection surface and returns the client to INR-first presentation with no data change
non_goals: The localization framework and INR rendering, which T-GLO-02 owns
Server-side conversion, rate sourcing and ledger currency policy, which T-GLO-01 and T-ADR-LEDGER-03 own
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo android. Owns the currency selection surface and multi-currency presentation only. Rates, conversion and stored amounts are server-owned and are never recomputed here.
